Find the chunks most relevant to a question

Source: R/retrieval.R
dragon_retrieve.Rd

Find the chunks most relevant to a question

Usage

dragon_retrieve(docs, query, k = 4, method = c("hybrid", "dense"), extra = 0)

Arguments

docs

A dragon_documents object or its directory. Indexed on the fly if it has no index yet.

query

One question, or several.

k

Chunks to return per query.

method

"hybrid" (the default) ranks chunks by combining the embedding similarity with a keyword (BM25) match, which catches exact terms and figures a small embedding model ranks too low; "dense" uses the embedding alone. On three document sets hybrid raised the share of questions whose source chunk was among the top four from 90.6 to 93.0, 88 to 100, and 91 to 100 percent.

extra

Chunks to add after the top k that say something different from those already chosen (relevant, but not near-copies). A rule that several documents repeat and one later document words differently is otherwise crowded out; the top k itself is unchanged.

Value

A data frame with one row per hit: query (when several), n (rank), id, source, section, page (PDFs), text, score (cosine similarity times the chunk's weight; rows are ordered by the combined ranking, so it need not decrease), similarity, and weight.

Examples

if (interactive()) {
docs <- dragon_documents(dragon_example_documents(), name = "policies")
dragon_retrieve(docs, "How long is the return window?", k = 3)
}
